canonical_name: Coupling method / synchronization of random systems (source topic label)

statement_blocker: The repository supplies only a technique label and a one-line synchronization gloss. It does not choose a stochastic model, probability/noise and state spaces, time domain, joint law or coupling construction, marginal constraints, synchronization predicate, hypotheses, quantifier order, convergence mode, rate, exceptional sets, or theorem conclusion. Selecting a coupling inequality, successful-coupling theorem, common-noise contraction, weak synchronization result, or singleton-attractor theorem would substitute missing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an exact source must fix universes and the probability/noise, state, and time types; measurable, metric, topological, order, or normed structures; the stochastic process, Markov kernel, random map, flow, cocycle, or stochastic equation; initial states; and regularity and filtration assumptions.
conclusion: Open: the source states no truth-valued conclusion, such as existence of a coupling with given marginals, finite-time coalescence, a coupling inequality, distance convergence in a specified mode, convergence to an invariant random point, or existence of a singleton random attractor.
candidate_scope_not_credited: a source-specified joint probability law with two prescribed marginals
a source-specified successful or coalescent coupling of two Markov processes
a source-specified coupling inequality for total variation, Wasserstein distance, or another metric
a source-specified common-noise pathwise contraction result
a source-specified weak synchronization theorem with convergence in probability to an invariant random point
a source-specified almost-sure synchronization theorem uniform over an initial-state class
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty or singleton state space and identical initial states
zero, finite, or infinite coupling time and trajectories that never meet
finite-time equality versus asymptotic distance zero
pseudometric zero without equality and infinite-valued distances
degenerate or absent noise, deterministic dynamics, and absorbing states
nonunique solutions and the distinction between weak and strong solution couplings
almost-sure, in-probability, in-expectation, and in-law convergence
pair-dependent exceptional sets versus one null set uniform over all initial states
excluded_substitutions: THM-M-1424 random dynamical systems, THM-M-1425 random attractors, and THM-M-1426 multivalued random dynamical systems
a generic Markov-chain mixing, ergodicity, invariant-measure, total-variation, or Wasserstein theorem

equality in distribution presented as samplewise equality or trajectory coalescence
a deterministic coupled-oscillator or network synchronization theorem
a one-state, constant-map, or otherwise tautological toy system
a numerical simulation, empirical synchronization plot, or unchecked stochastic solver
